### Childhood in Cairo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Childhood in Cairo")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Dalida_1937.jpg/250px-Dalida_1937.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dalida_1937.jpg)

Dalida in 1937, aged 4

Dalida was born Iolanda Cristina Gigliotti in [Cairo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cairo "Cairo"), [Kingdom of Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Egypt "Kingdom of Egypt"), on 17 January 1933. Her father Pietro Gigliotti (1904–1945) and mother Filomena Giuseppina ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")d'Alba; 1904–1971) were both born in [Serrastretta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serrastretta "Serrastretta"), [Calabria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calabria "Calabria"), Italy,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-histoire-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-aiello-12) and were then taken by their emigrant parents to Egypt.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-diacritik-13) Pietro studied music at school and played the violin in taverns; Giuseppina was a seamstress and homemaker.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-autogenerated1-14) By birth, Dalida automatically gained Italian nationality through _[jus sanguinis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jus\_sanguinis "Jus sanguinis")_ of both Italian parents. It has been suggested that Dalida had Jewish roots,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-aiello-12) with her family's hometown of Serrastretta having been founded by [Spanish Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Jews "Spanish Jews")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-edge-15) and her grandfather Enrico had [Algerian Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algerian_Jewish "Algerian Jewish") ancestry.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-aiello-12)

The year they were married, the Gigliottis settled in the [Shubra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shubra "Shubra") district of [Cairo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cairo "Cairo"), where, between the births of Iolanda's older brother Orlando (1930–1992) and younger brother [Bruno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Gigliotti "Bruno Gigliotti") (1936), the Gigliotti family [became well established in the community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutamassirun "Mutamassirun"). In addition to earnings from Giuseppina's work, their social status benefited when Pietro became [primo violino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concertmaster "Concertmaster") at Cairo's [Khedivial Opera House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khedivial_Opera_House "Khedivial Opera House"), and the family bought a two-storey house.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-histoire-11)

At 10 months old, Gigliotti caught an eye infection and had to wear bandages for 40 days. Her father would play [lullabies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lullaby "Lullaby") on the violin to soothe her. She underwent eye operations between the ages of three and five. Having to wear glasses throughout elementary school, for which she was bullied, she later recalled: "I was [_[sic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "Sic")_] enough of it, I would rather see the world in a blur than wear glasses, so I threw them through the window." Gigliotti attended the Scuola Tecnica Commerciale Maria Ausiliatrice, an Italian Catholic school located in northern Shubra.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-histoire-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-diacritik-13)

In 1940, [Allied forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II "Allies of World War II") took her father and other Italian men from their quarter to the Fayed prison camp in the desert near Cairo. When Pietro was released in 1944, he returned home a completely different person, so violent that Gigliotti and other children in the neighbourhood were scared of him. She later recalled, "I hated him when he beat me, I hated him especially when he beat my mom and brothers. I wanted him to die, and he did." Gigliotti was twelve when Pietro died of a [brain abscess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain_abscess "Brain abscess") in 1945.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-histoire-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-diacritik-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-autogenerated1-14)

### Modelling, acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Modelling, acting")]

In her teen years, Gigliotti developed an interest in acting due to her uncle's job as a projectionist for a local cinema, and often participated in school performances at the end of the semester. She graduated in 1951, and began working as a [copy typist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copy_typist "Copy typist") in a pharmaceutical company the same year. While required to work to financially help her family, Gigliotti still had acting ambitions.

Shortly thereafter, her best friend Miranda encouraged her to compete in Miss Ondine, a minor Cairo beauty pageant which she entered on the assurance that it was just for fun and that her mother would not find out. When Gigliotti unexpectedly won second prize and Miranda won second runner-up, they were photographed and the photographs were published in newspapers _Le journal d'Égypte_ and _Le progrès égyptien_. The next day, when her mother found out, she forcibly cut Gigliotti's hair short. Eventually, her mother relented and Gigliotti left her job to start modelling for Donna, a Cairo-based fashion house.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-Archived_copy-16)

Three [Egyptian film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_Egypt "Cinema of Egypt") directors cast Gigliotti in their productions: [Marco de Gastyne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_de_Gastyne "Marco de Gastyne") cast her in _The Mask of Tutankhamun_ (1954) and [Niazi Mostafa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niazi_Mostafa "Niazi Mostafa") cast her in a supporting role in _[A Glass and a Cigarette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Glass\_and\_a\_Cigarette "A Glass and a Cigarette")_ (1954),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-IMDb_Cigarette-17) on posters for which she appears with her newly adopted stage name Dalila (which she would soon change to "Dalida") because, as she explained in 1968, "it was a very frequent name in Egypt and I liked it a lot."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-18)

### Relocation to Paris and decisive 421 dice game

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Relocation to Paris and decisive 421 dice game")]

On 25 December 1954, Dalida left Egypt for Paris.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-19) Her first residence was a room in an apartment belonging to Gastyne's friend, the impresario Vidal. She met with a number of directors and auditioned for movie roles, but failed each time. Vidal relocated her to a smaller apartment, where her first neighbour was the actor [Alain Delon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alain_Delon "Alain Delon") (who at this time was still unknown to the wider public), with whom she had a brief relationship.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-20)

Dalida's difficulty in finding acting work throughout 1955 led her to try singing. Vidal introduced her to Roland Berger, a friend and professor who agreed to give her singing lessons seven days per week for a low fee. He was strict and used to yell, with Dalida responding even more loudly.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-21) Their lessons sometimes ended with her slamming the door, but she always returned the next day. Seeing her progress, Berger arranged for her to perform in the cabaret Le Drap d'Or on [Champs-Élysées](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champs-%C3%89lys%C3%A9es "Champs-Élysées"), where she was spotted by Jacques Paoli, the director of another cabaret, La Villa d'Este.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-autogenerated2-22) Paoli engaged her for a series of performances that proved to be popular, and Dalida received her first attention from the public in France, among whom was [Bruno Coquatrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Coquatrix "Bruno Coquatrix"), the director of [Olympia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympia_(Paris) "Olympia (Paris)"), who invited her to perform in his singing contest _Les Numéros 1 de demain_. Coquatrix later said: "[H]er voice is full of colour and volume, and has all that men love: gentleness, sensuality and eroticism." Dalida was also spotted by author and screenwriter Alfred Marchand, who advised to change her name to Dalida, since her pseudonym too closely resembled [the Biblical character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delilah "Delilah") as depicted in the movie _[Samson and Delilah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samson\_and\_Delilah\_(1949\_film) "Samson and Delilah (1949 film)")_. She immediately followed the advice.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-23)

On 9 April 1956, Dalida participated in the singing contest _Les Numéros 1 de demain_, performing "Etrangère au Paradis". Prior to the competition, [Eddie Barclay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Barclay "Eddie Barclay"), the owner of the largest record label in France, [Barclay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclay_(record_label) "Barclay (record label)"), and [Lucien Morisse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucien_Morisse?action=edit&redlink=1 "Lucien Morisse (page does not exist)")[[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucien%20Morisse "fr:Lucien Morisse")], the artistic director of the newly established radio station [Europe n°1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe_1 "Europe 1"), met in Bar Romain (now Petit Olympia) and discussed what to do that evening. Barclay wanted to watch a film, whereas Morisse wanted to attend the singing competition, which was being held at Olympia Hall, then the largest venue in Paris. They settled their disagreement by playing 421, a dice game, which Morisse won.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-24) Together with their friend Coquatrix, they were greatly impressed after Dalida won the contest, and arranged a meeting with her. This event was later revisited in [biopics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopic "Biopic") and books, and became regarded as fateful for Dalida's career. The three men went on to play a large part in launching her career.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-linternaute.com-25)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Career")]

### _Les années Barclay_ – The Barclay years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Les années Barclay – The Barclay years")]

#### First contract and overnight success with "Bambino"

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: First contract and overnight success with \"Bambino\"")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/Dalida_1950s_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Dalida_1950s_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dalida_1950s_(cropped).jpg)

Dalida in the 1950s

After the performance in _Les Numéros 1 de demain_, Morisse handed Dalida his card so that they could meet in his office as soon as possible, which she accepted without hesitation. A few days later, on the second floor of the building at 26 Rue François Ier, she performed "Barco negro", a recent hit by [Amália Rodrigues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Am%C3%A1lia_Rodrigues "Amália Rodrigues"), humming the a cappella verses and tapping her fingertips on a corner of Morisse's desk. Visibly satisfied, he demanded that she work on minor imperfections before a new audition in front of [Eddie Barclay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Barclay "Eddie Barclay") in person.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-26) On 2 May 1956 in Barclay's office at 20 Rue de Madrid, Dalida signed a renewable one-year contract, with a modest percentage on record sales, with the promise of increasing it if the expected success was accomplished.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-27) While Morisse was responsible for radio promotion, Coquatrix had developed a strategy to grab the headlines. He planned to promote her through a series of concerts, including two concerts at the [Olympia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympia_(Paris) "Olympia (Paris)"), two weeks in [Bobino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobino "Bobino"), and a tour of the provinces.

Her first song "Madona" was recorded in June and was first released in August on an EP with three other songs. "Madona" was played on 28 August 1956 on Radio Europe n°1, which was Dalida's first radio appearance.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:1-28) The record achieved sufficient success and was followed by a second EP, Le Torrent, a month later, which received an equally encouraging welcome. Dalida continued performing live throughout the latter part of 1956, while her promoters worked on developing a song that would make her a star; Morisse asked lyricist [Jacques Larue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Laurent "Jacques Laurent") to write a French language version of the [Neapolitan song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neapolitan_song "Neapolitan song") "[Guaglione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guaglione "Guaglione")", which had won at the recent inaugural [Festival di Napoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Festival_di_Napoli "Festival di Napoli") and would become "[Bambino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bambino_(song) "Bambino (song)")".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:1-28)

"Bambino" was released in early December only as a promo single, but quickly received more public interest than all of her previous recordings. Morisse started to heavily promote it and it was placed as the first track on Dalida's debut album _[Son nom est Dalida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son\_nom\_est\_Dalida "Son nom est Dalida")_, which was issued at the end of the same month.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:6-29) The album was immediately followed by a third EP titled _Bambino_. After debuting at number seven in January 1957,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-30)_Bambino_ reached number one and went on to become the biggest-selling and one of the most beloved pop standard hits of the 1950s in France, Belgium, Canada and Switzerland. As the song knocked [Doris Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doris_Day "Doris Day")'s "[Whatever Will Be, Will Be](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Que_Sera,_Sera_(Whatever_Will_Be,_Will_Be) "Que Sera, Sera (Whatever Will Be, Will Be)")" off the top of the French charts,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-31) women began to emulate Dalida's makeup, resulting in an explosion of [Rimmel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rimmel "Rimmel") sales, while men saw in her a talent, sensuality and sexiness. [Coquatrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Coquatrix "Bruno Coquatrix") then named her "the first sex-symbol of the song".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:2-32) "Bambino" was Dalida's first number-one hit, and through 1957 it became the longest-running number one in world history, with a total of 39 consecutive weeks, a record that it still holds.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:3-33) It made Dalida an overnight star and gave her her first gold disc, the very first time that such an award had been received by a woman, on 19 September 1957 for sales of over 300,000.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:1-28) As the French music industry was then still in the background, "Bambino" was described in 2007 by Bertrand Dicale of [Le Figaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Figaro "Le Figaro") as "a launch that announced what will happen in the coming decades ... a start of really modern times where singer is more important than song".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-34) Promoting it in early 1957, Dalida also made her first TV appearance, and her contract was immediately extended for four years.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-35) Then she also received her first criticism from a journalist: "On stage, Dalida appears in beauty and warmth, highlighted by a presentation of extreme sobriety."

#### First Olympia concert, new success with "Gondolier", tourings and return to film

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: First Olympia concert, new success with \"Gondolier\", tourings and return to film")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Dalida_1957.jpg/250px-Dalida_1957.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dalida_1957.jpg)

Dalida in 1957

On the night of 27 February 1957, Dalida held her first concert at the Olympia, as the opening act for [Charles Aznavour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Aznavour "Charles Aznavour"), and was widely applauded.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:8-36) Then, in April, she performed a successful two-week series of concerts at Bobino, and in the summer a fan club was established, the first such club to be devoted to a female artist.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:4-38) As well as live performances, the prolonged success of "Bambino" through 1957 was followed with new recordings such as "Miguel" and "Tu n'as pas très bon caractère", which eventually replaced "Bambino" as number one in France in October.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-39) Dalida came back to the Olympia in September as the opening act for [Gilbert Bécaud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_B%C3%A9caud "Gilbert Bécaud"); the newly renovated Olympia having just acquired its red neon facade sign. A future iconic symbol of the hall, Bécaud and Dalida became the first two names to appear on it.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:15-40) After her second success there, Dalida released her second album _[Miguel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel\_(album) "Miguel (album)")_ and returned to the studio in mid-October to record what was to become one of her old standards, "Histoire d'un amour". Staying in the top ten for eight months, it earned Dalida a second gold disc.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:7-41)

Dalida's experimentation with exotica resulted in "[Gondolier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gondolier_(song) "Gondolier (song)")", released for Christmas 1957. For this exotic song with accentuated vocals, Dalida delivered a TV appearance where, while sailing an imaginary [gondola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gondola "Gondola"), the shoulder strap of her dress fell down.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-42) The reappearance of this video in the 1970s made the moment notable, and the public started to consider it iconic that Dalida dared to do such a thing on television during such a conventional time in society.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:9-43) Nevertheless, "Gondolier" debuted at number one in both the French and Canadian charts, where it spent four months, remaining in the top twenty for almost a year and becoming her biggest hit since "Bambino".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:3-33) Its B side "Pardon" also proved popular, reaching number one in Canada.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:0-44) Dalida then also started to perform more frequently in France, Belgium and Luxembourg.

By the end of April 1958, a radio programmer heard Dalida recording "[Dans le bleu du ciel bleu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volare_(song) "Volare (song)")" in Barclay's Hoche studios in Paris. After immediately asking for a copy of the tape and broadcasting it, the radio station was swamped with phone calls from people asking for the number of the disc and when it would be available.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-45) As the song replaced "Gondolier" as number one in France, Dalida scored a still-current chart record in France of five songs simultaneously in the top ten.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-46) It was followed by her receipt of RMC's singer of the year award, which she went on to win for six consecutive years.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:10-47) In June she embarked upon her first "TDF avec Dalida 58" tour ([Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_de_France "Tour de France") with Dalida), with a daily appearance in the city hosting each stage of the [1958 Tour de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_Tour_de_France "1958 Tour de France"), which she repeated several time in future decades. She also performed in [Algiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algiers "Algiers") during the summer, supporting the morale of French soldiers fighting the [Algerian War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algerian_War "Algerian War"), and held a new series of galas in France and Belgium that regularly ended with two hours of autograph signing.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:5-48) During this summer Dalida released her third album _[Gondolier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gondolier\_(album) "Gondolier (album)")_, and also recorded several new songs such as "Je pars", "Aïe mon cœur" and "Les Gitans"; all of which were sales successes, each earning Dalida a gold disc. With "Je pars", Dalida started French [rock 'n' roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") and also paved the way for foreign rock artists to enter the market, such as [Paul Anka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Anka "Paul Anka").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-49)

In late 1958, Dalida returned to film in her first on-screen role in four years, playing the supporting role of a singer-spy in the mystery film _Rapt au deuxième bureau_. A few months later, she appeared alongside Eddie Barclay in _Brigade des mœurs_, both starring as themselves. These two B movies were also used for promotion of her three songs "Inconnue mon amour", "L'amour chante", and "Aime-moi", and were released in September 1958 and March 1959, respectively.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-50)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-51)

On 9 October, she again performed at Bobino, this time for three weeks as the headline performer, where she promoted her latest releases "Du moment qu'on s'aime", which peaked in the charts the same week, and "[Come prima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_prima "Come prima")". Topping the charts in January 1959, where it remained over most of the winter, "Come prima" proved to be an ultimate holiday hit in France and Belgium, as Dalida could be seen promoting it on a Christmas-themed television set.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:3-33) The record's B side "Si je pouvais revivre un jour ma vie" also achieved success, topping the Canadian charts.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:0-44) According to her biographer [Catherine Rihoit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Rihoit "Catherine Rihoit"), her live television appearances "got her into the palms of society, keeping her position as a favorite singer of all age groups in the francophonie", and marked an era of late 1950s television shows.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:4-38) On 26 December 1958 Dalida was in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") with Morisse where they met [Norman Granz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Granz "Norman Granz"), the American impresario of [Ella Fitzgerald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ella_Fitzgerald "Ella Fitzgerald"), who invited her to [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles") and offered a fifteen-year contract to launch her career in the United States. She quickly rejected the offer, saying that she wanted to focus on her musical career in France where she was already well known with a secure fan base.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:2-32)

#### "Am Tag als der Regen kam" and international recognition; best selling singer in Europe

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: \"Am Tag als der Regen kam\" and international recognition; best selling singer in Europe")]

Dalida toured extensively in 1959, playing sold-out dates in France, Egypt, Italy and Germany.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:5-48) As her fame spread outside France, she started to record songs in other languages to cater for these new audiences. She understood five languages and interpreted her songs in eleven languages: [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language"), [Egyptian Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_Arabic "Egyptian Arabic"), [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language"), [Lebanese Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanese_Arabic "Lebanese Arabic"), [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"), [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"), [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language "Greek language"), [Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_language "Hebrew language"), [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"), [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_language "Japanese language") and [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_language "Dutch language"). In February, during a TV appearance, she performed her recent version of "[Hava Nagila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hava_Nagila "Hava Nagila")".[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-52) On 2 March, the [Minister of informations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Information_(France) "Minister of Information (France)") awarded her, alongside [Yves Montand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yves_Montand "Yves Montand"), with the Bravos du music hall, the most prestigious music award in France, as the most popular singer in France.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-53) During the summer, she covered her own recordings "Ne joue pas" and "C'est ça l'amore" in [Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_dialects "Flemish dialects") as "Speel niet met m'n hart" and "Ik zing amore", respectively, the only time in her career that she sang in Flemish.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:6-29)

In late summer, Dalida was back in the studio to record her first major international hit. In the period from 1958 to 1959, "[Le Jour où la pluie viendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Day_the_Rains_Came_(song) "The Day the Rains Came (song)")" was recorded in three languages, propelling Dalida straight into the top three in six different European countries. The German-language version "Am Tag als der Regen kam" topped the German charts for ten weeks in September and October, earning her another gold disc. It was the best-selling record of the year in Germany, and remains one of the most successful songs in the history of the country.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-54) During the closing night of the [Berlin Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_International_Film_Festival "Berlin International Film Festival") on 28 September 1959, she was presented with a Golden Lion award by RTL as the best-selling musical artist of the year in Germany, and was saluted with a fanfare playing the verses of "Am Tag als der Regen kam".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:2-32) The song was her first international hit, reaching half a million accumulated copies and remaining one of her greatest successes in Germany.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:7-41)

During the course of 1959, Dalida scored five Top 10 hits in French charts, most notably "[Ciao, ciao Bambina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piove_(Ciao,_ciao_bambina) "Piove (Ciao, ciao bambina)")" and "Guitare et Tambourin"; both of which earned gold discs. In Italy, [RAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAI "RAI") awarded her with Oscar di popolarità and Golden Wolf awards as the best-selling musical artist of the year in the country.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:7-41) These were her first two foreign awards and furthered her international recognition. Dalida also performed in successful sold-out concerts in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"), [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens") and Cairo, delivering a sentimental performance in front of a crowd in the Rivoli cinema that she frequented as a child.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:11-55) On 23 September 1959, Dalida sang in a successful three-week run at Parisian [Théâtre de l'Étoile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Th%C3%A9%C3%A2tre_de_l'%C3%89toile_(Champs-%C3%89lys%C3%A9es) "Théâtre de l'Étoile (Champs-Élysées)"), where a jukebox was installed in recognition of her being dubbed "Mademoiselle Jukebox", the most listened-to artist on [jukeboxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jukebox "Jukebox") in France.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-56) By the end of the year, she had released her fifth and sixth albums, _Le Disque d'or de Dalida_ and _[Love in Portofino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_in\_Portofino\_(album) "Love in Portofino (album)")_ (titled after her hit song "[Love in Portofino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_in_Portofino "Love in Portofino")"), and had already sold three and a half million records, the highest sales of all European artists.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-57)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Dalida_1961.jpg/250px-Dalida_1961.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dalida_1961.jpg)

Dalida in 1961

#### "Les Enfants du Pirée" and "Itsi bitsi petit bikini"; transition to yé-yé and first Olympia concert residency

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: \"Les Enfants du Pirée\" and \"Itsi bitsi petit bikini\"; transition to yé-yé and first Olympia concert residency")]

Dalida began 1960 with "[T'aimer follement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makin'_Love "Makin' Love")", which became a chart-topper in France and Belgium in February.[_[dead link](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Link\_rot "Wikipedia:Link rot")_][[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:16-58) She then embarked upon her first world tour and reached the summit of the charts again with "[Romantica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantica_(song) "Romantica (song)")" in April. Her third release of the year "[Les Enfants du Pirée](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_Enfants_du_Pir%C3%A9e "Les Enfants du Pirée")" brought Dalida huge commercial success, becoming her second biggest international hit after "Am Tag als der Regen kam". It reached the top two in six European countries and in Canada, topping the charts in three of them.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:12-59) After its debut at the top of the French charts in June 1960, where it remained for 20 weeks, it became the first song by a French singer to sell over one million copies internationally, and the expression _tube de l'été_ ("hit of the summer") was invented after its success.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:4-38) Dalida eventually recorded it in five different languages and made a video to be shown on TV, _Toute la Chanson_. With a harbor theme, it showed Dalida singing and lying on a fishing net with a wind machine blowing, and journalist [Jacques Chancel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Chancel "Jacques Chancel") called it "the first video in France that really made a shift from the era of outdated videos".[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-60)

The success was followed by her second Italian award Oscar di popolarità and a Golden Wolf as the best-selling musical artist of the year.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:1-28) Back in France, Dalida was not pleased by the emergence of the new musical style [yé-yé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y%C3%A9-y%C3%A9 "Yé-yé"), as the new singers would only briefly occupy the charts and then disappear. Also, since the appearance of new radio programs for youth such as _[Salut les copains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salut\_les\_copains\_(radio\_program) "Salut les copains (radio program)")_, both music-hall songs and singers, such as Dalida, began to be regarded as obsolete.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-61) Dalida realized that she would have to make a drastic change to retain her image, and in September she covered the US hit "[Itsi bitsi petit bikini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itsy_Bitsy_Teenie_Weenie_Yellow_Polkadot_Bikini "Itsy Bitsy Teenie Weenie Yellow Polkadot Bikini")". Now one of her signature songs, it became the first big yé-yé hit in France and became the second song to receive the title _tube de l'été_, displacing "Les Enfants du Pirée" from the top of the charts. Securing her position as a leading singer in France, "Itsi bitsi petit bikini" introduced Dalida to a whole new generation of young fans. Topping the charts across Western Europe and in Canada, the record was also her second to sell over a million and gained her a thirteenth golden disc.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:9-43)

This success was followed by "[Milord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milord_(song) "Milord (song)")", a number one in Austria, Germany and Italy, after which [her first album issued solely for the Italian public](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milord_(album) "Milord (album)") was named.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-62) Dalida then completed a year-long world tour, performing in countries across Europe, in Canada and in several Arab states. In December, she issued an EP _Joyeux Noël_ collecting four of the best-known holiday carols in French, and her New Year's show _Réveillon de Paris_ broke the record for a TV audience, with nearly six million viewers.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:8-36)

In January 1961, Dalida covered [The Drifters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Drifters "The Drifters")' "[Save the last dance for me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_the_Last_Dance_for_Me "Save the Last Dance for Me")" as "Garde-moi la dernière danse", reaching the top two. It remained her biggest French hit of the year as she undertook another year-long world tour, which started in [Tehran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehran "Tehran") on 18 February in front of the Iranian royal family in their [Sa'dabad Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sa'dabad_Complex "Sa'dabad Complex").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:1-28) With a total of almost 200 dates, the last leg of the tour included Dalida's first own concert residency at the Olympia, which started on 6 December. Due to her recent love affair, her divorce from Morisse and her new yé-yé direction, several critics announced this to be "attestment of an end and downfall of Dalida". Dalida "brought the house down" according to Beuve-Méry of _[Le Monde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Monde "Le Monde")_; the month-long show was a sell-out success, with the first night being broadcast live by Radio Europe N°1.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-63) Among other musicians who attended, she was congratulated by [Édith Piaf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89dith_Piaf "Édith Piaf"), who told her: "You are a winner, like me. After me, it will be you."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:4-38) Dalida also set the record for the largest public attendance and the longest-running concert residency at the Olympia, with a total of 52,000 spectators over the course of 30 days, a record that she would break herself in 1981.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:5-48) At the end of the year, on 30 December, Dalida completed her world tour at the [Ancienne Belgique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancienne_Belgique "Ancienne Belgique") in [Bruxelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels"), Olympia's Belgian equivalent.

During 1961, Dalida issued a set of new Italian songs on the _[Canta in italiano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canta\_in\_Italiano\_(Dalida\_album) "Canta in Italiano (Dalida album)")_ EP, and also scored several top ten hits internationally such as "Nuits d'Espagne" and "Tu ne sais pas". In April "Pépé" became a number one hit both in Austria and Germany, while "[24 mille baisers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24.000_baci "24.000 baci")" charted separately in Austria and France.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-64) She also issued two albums _[Dalida internationale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida\_internationale "Dalida internationale")_ and _[Loin de moi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loin\_de\_moi "Loin de moi")_. During the spring in Italy, Dalida signed with film director [Giorgio Simonelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgio_Simonelli "Giorgio Simonelli") and revived her film career with the first film in which she plays the main role. Originally titled _Che femmina... e che dollari!_, it was revoiced and retitled for a French audience as _Parlez-moi d'amour_, after [one of the soundtrack songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parlez-moi_d'amour_(song) "Parlez-moi d'amour (song)"). The movie also features several other recordings by Dalida, including the posthumously released "Ho trovato la felicità". In contrast to her other previous movies, _Che femmina... e che dollari!_ was not a commercial failure, with the moderate gross income eventually surpassing the low budget.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-65) Rihoit wrote: "sealing her appearance of the early 60's, since it is also her first color film, all the power and acting potential that Dalida carries in herself and transmits to the screen is clearly visible".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:4-38)

#### "La Leçon de Twist", "Le Petit Gonzales", exhaustive tours and scopitones

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: \"La Leçon de Twist\", \"Le Petit Gonzales\", exhaustive tours and scopitones")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/Dalida_and_Chet_Baker_2.jpg/250px-Dalida_and_Chet_Baker_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dalida_and_Chet_Baker_2.jpg)

Dalida with [Chet Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chet_Baker "Chet Baker") on 13 April 1961, Italy

After a short break Dalida was back on tour, this time starting in Canada where "Tu peux le prendre" had reached number one.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:0-44) On 5 February, on the popular French youth TV program _Toute la Chanson_, Dalida performed her latest yé-yé release "La Leçon de Twist". Accompanied on the piano by then leading French teen idol [Johnny Hallyday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Hallyday "Johnny Hallyday"), he also taught Dalida the dance moves, about what she said: "he really showed himself, the most friendly of teachers of this new rhythm".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:2-32) The performance caused a sensation, rocketing her track straight to the top of French and Belgian charts.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:13-66) "La Leçon de Twist" was followed by another success in the same genre "Achète-moi un juke-box", with the lyrics "Oh dad, buy me a jukebox, to listen to [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley"), [Les Chaussettes Noires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_Chaussettes_Noires "Les Chaussettes Noires"), and [Johnny Hallyday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Hallyday "Johnny Hallyday") – And Dalida? But what is she doing here, they still listen to her?",[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-67) Dalida was making a joke at her own expense referring to the current situation in France where the young people were fond of young singers, despite her success during the yé-yé era. The record spent two weeks at number one during the spring.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:13-66)

From April to July Dalida toured Italy and [Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam "Vietnam"). In [Saigon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho_Chi_Minh_City "Ho Chi Minh City"), her popularity led to traffic congestion when she performed, but the local authorities interrupted her show during a rendition of "La Leçon de Twist" because the song was considered to be a political act.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:8-36) In May Dalida was back at the top of the international charts with "Le Petit Gonzales", a cover of "[Speedy Gonzales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Gonzales_(song) "Speedy Gonzales (song)")", which peaked in France, Belgium, Canada and [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain") the following month and remains known as "one of the most memorable and nostalgic recordings of the yé-yé era", according to _[Le Parisien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Parisien "Le Parisien")_ in 1987.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-68) The [album of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_petit_Gonzales "Le petit Gonzales") was issued later in the year.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:14-69)

Although Dalida had filmed her first [scopitone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scopitone "Scopitone") in 1961 for the song "Loin de moi", starting a series of music videos that were followed by almost all yé-yé newcomers, her best critically and commercially received scopitone was recorded in September 1962 for the song "Le Jour le plus long", in which she paid tribute to the [Allies' disembarkation in Normandy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normandy_landings "Normandy landings") on 6 June 1944.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:1-28) Under the direction of the young [Claude Lelouch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Lelouch "Claude Lelouch"), who later became one of the most acclaimed French directors, Dalida dressed as a soldier and walked through a war-torn forest in the middle of bombing accompanied by real scenes from the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"). This unusual image of Dalida found an audience and was a hit in cafes. Alongside Dalida's performance of the song on 26 September, in front of a crowd of 2,000 people on the first floor of the [Eiffel Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiffel_Tower "Eiffel Tower"), "Le Jour le plus long" topped charts in France for two weeks and earned her another gold disc.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:11-55)

#### More concentration on concerts, shift to pop; "Eux", "Amore scusami" and first platinum disc

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dalida&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: More concentration on concerts, shift to pop; \"Eux\", \"Amore scusami\" and first platinum disc")]

Dalida spent 1963 making live appearance all over the world and dedicating herself more to the young Canadian public, as yé-yé was experiencing its greatest success in France during this period. Her world tour was a success, with sold-out concerts in Europe from Portugal to Poland, Canada, Asia, [Fort-de-France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort-de-France "Fort-de-France"), Latin America and Arabian countries. In Algeria, she became the first artist to appear since the [proclamation of independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algerian_independence "Algerian independence").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:5-48) Dalida also dedicated the late summer period to filming, spending three months in Hong Kong filming in the B movie _L'Inconnue de Hong-Kong_ in which she starred alongside [Serge Gainsbourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serge_Gainsbourg "Serge Gainsbourg"). Although the movie was a commercial flop, Dalida received favorable reviews.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-70)

In January 1963 at [Cortina d'Ampezzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortina_d'Ampezzo "Cortina d'Ampezzo"), Dalida was awarded with the Oscar Mondiale del Successo dei Juke Box award for the most listened artist on [jukeboxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jukebox "Jukebox") in Europe.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-71) Later the same month, she made a shift from yé-yé in covering [Ben E. King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_E._King "Ben E. King")'s "[Stand by Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stand_by_Me_(Ben_E._King_song) "Stand by Me (Ben E. King song)")" as "Tu croiras", which was followed by an equally melancholic string of recordings such as "Le Jour du retour", a summer number one hit in Canada, and "Eux" which subsequently peaked at number two in [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina "Argentina") and was recorded in five languages. "Eux" was awarded the Oscar mundial du success du disque for the most international sales by a French artist in 1963, and Dalida named her fourteenth studio [album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida_discography#Studio_albums "Dalida discography") after it.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:9-43)

The 1963 world tour was extended into 1964 with only a few short breaks. The French leg of the tour started on 11 April 1964, during which Dalida traveled 30,000 kilometers solely by car over its five-month run, and had a public attendance in excess of 200,000. "The most iconic moment of the tour," according to her brother Orlando, was a concert at [Draguignan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draguignan "Draguignan") on 14 August when "Dalida appeared with blond hair for the first time, and shocked the crowd that didn't recognize her at first glance."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-72)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:5-48) After the concert in [Pont-sur-Yonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pont-sur-Yonne "Pont-sur-Yonne") on 2 September, Dalida accepted the offer of local truck drivers to become their godmother of honor. The tour was followed by a concert residency in the Olympia two days later when Dalida and other celebrities, [Charles Aznavour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Aznavour "Charles Aznavour"), [Françoise Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7oise_Hardy "Françoise Hardy"), Johnny Hallyday and [Sylvie Vartan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvie_Vartan "Sylvie Vartan"), were conveyed to the entrance of the Olympia by the same drivers on open trucks, forming a parade through the streets of Paris.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-73) The event generated even more interest in the sold-out three-week residency, which had already received a huge amount of media coverage. During the television transmission of the crowd at the entrance, a teenage fan said: "We can hardly wait for her [Dalida] to appear, we've been screaming for an hour and the atmosphere is so crazy", upon which the reporter turned to the camera, saying "the whole of Paris came to see [the parade], only in front of the Olympia there are at least 2,000 people waiting in the street".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:9-43)

As Dalida was recording simultaneously with her concerts during the course of 1964, releases such as "Ce coin de terre", "Ne t'en fais pas pour ça" and "Chaque instant de" were poorly promoted on TV, eventually only entering the top twenty. "Là il a dit" had peaked at number six in Canada earlier in the year, but on finishing the tour in November, Dalida returned to the studio to record "[Amore scusami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amore_scusami "Amore scusami")", an orchestral sentimental pop ballad, which was a completely new genre in her repertoire. The song was rush-released and swiftly became a hit at the end of the year, earning Dalida another gold disc, the first in two years following "Le Jour le plus long".[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:17-74) Following the success of "Amore scusami", an [album of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amore_scusami_(album) "Amore scusami (album)") was released on 17 September. Dalida was awarded with a platinum disc for surpassing sales of over 10 million records since her debut in 1956.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:14-69)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-75) Specifically created for her, this was the first time in the music industry that the term "[platinum disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_disc "Platinum disc")" had been used.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:7-41)

Refusing to perform at [Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival "Sanremo Music Festival"), Dalida instead released the EP _Sanremo 65_ that included her latest Italian top ten hit "Ascoltami". With new performances at Bobino and Tête de l'Art in the following months, Dalida was in the top ten in France and Belgium with a cover of [Rita Pavone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Pavone "Rita Pavone")'s "[Viva la pappa col pomodoro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viva_la_pappa_col_pomodoro "Viva la pappa col pomodoro")" that gained huge interest among children.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-76) The B side "La Sainte Totoche", written and composed by Charles Aznavour, peaked at number six in Turkey and was applauded by _Lettres françaises_, who wrote "Sainte Totoche enters the calendar" as it "evokes the women neglected by their husbands".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-:2-32) Back on world tour in 1965, Dalida held concerts in Fort-de-France where she was welcomed by more than 20,000 enthusiastic Martinicans. [France-Antilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France-Antilles "France-Antilles") reported that "only the President of the Republic had an ovation of this scale, during his visit in March 1964".[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-77)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-78) The next day, Dalida herself rewarded Juliana Brown, the winner of the _Dalida Song Contest_ which had been established in her honour.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-79) In a poll conducted by [IFOP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institut_fran%C3%A7ais_d'opinion_publique "Institut français d'opinion publique") on 24 April 1965 Dalida was voted the favourite French singer of the decade, ahead of Édith Piaf.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalida#cite_note-80)
