American singer and actress Rosemary Clooney grew up in Maysville, Kentucky, the daughter of Marie Frances (Guilfoyle) and Andrew Joseph Clooney. She and her sister [Betty Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0167038/?ls) used to sing in her grandfather's Maysville mayoral election campaigns, which he won three times. Rosemary made her singing debut on Cincinnati radio station WLW in 1941 at 13. On WLW she worked with band leader Barney Rapp, who had also worked with [Doris Day](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000013/?ls) and [Andy Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0930023/?ls) at the same station. She attended high school at Our Lady of Mercy in Cincinnati. In 1946 she appeared with her sister in Atlantic City, New Jersey, at the Steel Pier with [Tony Pastor](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0665088/?ls)'s band. In 1949 she went solo and later appeared in [White Christmas (1954)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0047673/?ls), co-starring opposite [Bing Crosby](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001078/?ls) and [Danny Kaye](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001414/?ls). Her first big hit was "Come On A My House" in 1951. She married [José Ferrer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001207/?ls) in 1953 and they had five children between 1955 and 1960. Her marriage to Ferrer was a tempestuous one and she had a nervous breakdown in 1968, but went on to resume her career in 1976. Her life was dramatized in a 1982 made-for-television movie starring [Sondra Locke](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0516800/?ls), who was actually just 16 years Rosemary's junior but constantly lied about her age.  
  
Her son Gabriel is married to singer [Debby Boone](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0095501/?ls), daughter of 1950s pop singer [Pat Boone](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004769/?ls). Her brother, [Nick Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0167040/?ls), was an ABC news anchor in Cincinnati, and her nephew [George Clooney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000123/?ls) has developed into one of the biggest movie stars of the 21st century. In 1968 she was standing in the Ambassdor Hotel in Los Angeles with [Roosevelt Grier](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0340952/?ls) when [Robert F. Kennedy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0448305/?ls) was assassinated in the hotel kitchen after she had participated in his campaign rally. Her top hits include "Hey There" in 1954, "Tenderly", "This Ole House" and "Half As Much" in 1952.

    *   Music Artist
    *   Actor
    *   Producer

[The Dean Martin Show (1965–1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058797/?ref_=ls_knf_5)

Martin was born Dino Paul Crocetti in Steubenville, Ohio, to Gaetano Alfonso "Guy" Crocetti, an Italian immigrant and barber, and his Ohio-born wife, Angela (Barra) Crocetti. He spoke only Italian until age five. Martin came up the hard way, with such jobs as a boxer ("Kid Crochet"), a steel mill worker, a gas station worker and a casino croupier/dealer. In 1946, Martin got his first ticket to stardom, as he teamed up with another hard worker who was also trying to succeed in Hollywood: [Jerry Lewis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001471/?ls). Films such as [At War with the Army (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042209/?ls) sent the team toward super-stardom. The duo were to become one of Hollywood's truly great teams. They lasted 11 years together, and starred in 16 movies. They were unstoppable, but personality conflicts broke up the team. Even without Lewis, Martin was a true superstar.  
  
Few thought that Martin would go on to achieve solo success, but he did, winning critical acclaim for his role in [The Young Lions (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052415/?ls) with [Marlon Brando](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000008/?ls) and [Montgomery Clift](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001050/?ls), and [Some Came Running (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052218/?ls), with [Shirley MacLaine](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000511/?ls) and [Frank Sinatra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000069/?ls). Movies such as [Rio Bravo (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053221/?ls) brought him international fame. One of his best remembered films is in [Ocean's Eleven (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054135/?ls), in which he played Sam Harmon alongside the other members of the legendary Rat Pack: [Frank Sinatra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000069/?ls), [Sammy Davis Jr.](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002035/?ls), [Joey Bishop](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0084086/?ls) and [Peter Lawford](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0492444/?ls). Martin proved potent at the box office through the 1960s, with films such as [Bells Are Ringing (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053645/?ls) and [Robin and the 7 Hoods (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058529/?ls), again with Rat Pack pals [Sammy Davis Jr.](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002035/?ls) and Sinatra. During much of the 1960s and 1970s, his film persona of a boozing playboy prompted a series of films as secret agent Matt Helm and his own television variety show. [Airport (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065377/?ls) followed, featuring Martin as a pilot. He played a phony priest in [The Cannonball Run (1981)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0082136/?ls).  
  
In 1965, Martin explored a new method for entertaining his fans: Television. That year he hosted one of the most successful TV series in history: [The Dean Martin Show (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058797/?ls), which lasted until 1973. In 1965, it won a Golden Globe Award. In 1973, he renamed it "The Dean Martin Comedy Hour", and from 1974 to 1984 it was renamed again, this time "The Dean Martin Celebrity Roasts". It became one of the most successful TV series in history, skewering such greats as [Bob Hope](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001362/?ls), [Frank Sinatra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000069/?ls), [Lucille Ball](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000840/?ls), [James Stewart](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000071/?ls), [George Burns](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0122675/?ls), [Milton Berle](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000926/?ls), [Don Rickles](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0725543/?ls), [Phyllis Diller](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0226887/?ls), and [Joe Namath](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0620619/?ls).  
  
His last public role was a return to the stage, for a cross-country concert tour with Davis and Sinatra. He spoke affectionately of his fellow Rat Packers. "The satisfaction that I get out of working with these two bums is that we have more laughs than the audience has", Martin said. After the 1980s, Martin took it easy until his son, [Dean Paul Martin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0552162/?ls), was killed in a plane crash in March 1987.  
  
Devastated by the loss, from which he never recovered, he walked out on a reunion tour with Sinatra and Davis. Martin spent his final years in solitude, out of the public light. A heavy smoker most of his life, Martin died on Christmas Day 1995 at age 78 from complications to lung cancer.

Her debut album Songs of Love (1979) followed, with a quick sophomore effort Sweet Surrender, but no follow-up matched its success, cementing her one-hit wonder status. [![Image 7: Anita Ward, born December 20, 1956, in Memphis, Tennessee, is an American disco and R&B singer forever linked to her iconic 1979 smash “Ring My Bell”. The oldest of five children to minister James L. Ward and homemaker Juanita Ward, she grew up singing in church choirs from age nine, developing a love for gospel that shaped her powerful, soulful voice. Ward pursued higher education at Rust College, a historically Black college in Holly Springs, Mississippi. There, she earned a Bachelor of Arts in psychology in 1978, sang in the renowned a cappella choir (which toured internationally and recorded with opera legend Leontyne Price), and performed with a gospel quartet. Initially aspiring to a “normal” life as an elementary school substitute teacher in Memphis, Ward’s talent led her manager (met during a Godspell audition at Rust) to connect her with producer Frederick Knight in Jackson, Mississippi. Knight reworked a teen-themed song into the adult-oriented disco anthem “Ring My Bell,” originally intended for another artist. Released on his Juana label (distributed by TK Records), it exploded to #1 on the Billboard Hot 100, R&B, and Dance charts in the U.S., U.K., and Canada—selling millions and defining late-disco era. Her debut album Songs of Love (1979) followed, with a quick sophomore effort Sweet Surrender, but no follow-up matched its success, cementing her one-hit wonder status. After a serious car accident in the 1980s and shifting priorities, Ward returned to a quieter life in Memphis, occasionally performing. **Gino Paoli** (Italian pronunciation:[[ˈdʒiːno ˈpaːoli]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); 23 September 1934 – 24 March 2026) was an Italian singer-songwriter. He wrote a number of songs widely regarded as classics in [Italian popular music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_popular_music "Italian popular music"), including "[Il cielo in una stanza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il_cielo_in_una_stanza_(song) "Il cielo in una stanza (song)")", "Che cosa c'è", "[Senza fine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senza_fine "Senza fine")", "Quattro amici" and "[Sapore di sale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapore_di_sale "Sapore di sale")".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Paoli was born in [Monfalcone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monfalcone "Monfalcone"), near [Trieste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trieste "Trieste"), on 23 September 1934. He moved to [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa") as a child, where he spent all his life.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

After several different jobs, Paoli was signed to [Dischi Ricordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dischi_Ricordi "Dischi Ricordi") with friends and fellow musicians [Luigi Tenco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Tenco "Luigi Tenco") and [Bruno Lauzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Lauzi "Bruno Lauzi"), who would constitute, along with Paoli, [Umberto Bindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umberto_Bindi "Umberto Bindi"), [Giorgio Calabrese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgio_Calabrese "Giorgio Calabrese") and other artists, what is known as the "[Genoese School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoese_School "Genoese School")" of Italian songwriting.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2) His first success was the single "[La gatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_gatta "La gatta")", which has been used in Italian language teaching classes in U.S. middle schools and high schools.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

"[Il cielo in una stanza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il_cielo_in_una_stanza_(song) "Il cielo in una stanza (song)")" was composed in 1959. According to Paoli, the lyrics came to him while lying on a brothel bed. Gazing at the purple ceiling, he thought, "Love can grow at any moment at any place."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-3)[Mina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mina_(Italian_singer) "Mina (Italian singer)")'s single release of the song topped the list of annual sales in Italy[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-4) and reached the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). Video performances of the song were included in the movies _Io bacio... tu baci_ and _[Appuntamento a Ischia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appuntamento\_a\_Ischia "Appuntamento a Ischia")_. It was later featured in _[Goodfellas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas "Goodfellas")_. [Carla Bruni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carla_Bruni "Carla Bruni") covered the song (mixing French with her native Italian) on her debut album _[Quelqu'un m'a dit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quelqu'un\_m'a\_dit "Quelqu'un m'a dit")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Paoli's debut [album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album "Album"), _Gino Paoli_, was released in Italy on 8 October 1961 on Dischi Ricordi.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-5) "Il cielo in una stanza" was followed by "[Sapore di sale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapore_di_sale "Sapore di sale")" (1963), arranged by [Ennio Morricone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ennio_Morricone "Ennio Morricone") and considered to be one of Paoli's most famous songs. In the same year he attempted suicide by shooting himself to the heart (the bullet remained inside his chest).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1974, he returned with the LP _I semafori rossi non sono Dio_, followed by _Il mio mestiere_ (1977). Both showed a more mature inspiration than his 1960s works. In the 1980s, Paoli produced a series of successful albums, and in 1985, he toured Italy together with [Ornella Vanoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornella_Vanoni "Ornella Vanoni").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1987, he [was elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Italian_general_election "1987 Italian general election") to the [Italian Chamber of Deputies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Chamber_of_Deputies "Italian Chamber of Deputies") for the [Italian Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Communist_Party "Italian Communist Party"), soon withdrawing from the party to become a left-wing independent.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-6) He abandoned politics in 1992 to pursue his musical ambitions.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Paoli had several relationships during his lifetime. He first married Anna Fabbri in 1957, with whom he had a son. After separating, he had a long relationship with actress [Stefania Sandrelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefania_Sandrelli "Stefania Sandrelli") in the 1960s; their daughter, [Amanda Sandrelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Sandrelli "Amanda Sandrelli"), is also an actress. He subsequently had an affair with singer [Ornella Vanoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornella_Vanoni "Ornella Vanoni"), who remained a close friend of his throughout their lives. Finally, he began dating Paola Penzo of [Modena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modena "Modena") in the 1970s, marrying her in 1991; the couple had three sons.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto2-7)

### Legal issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Legal issues")]

During an interview in February 2015, when a journalist cited a famous phrase of an Italian minister saying that taxes are a good thing, Paoli insulted him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-8) At the time Paoli was under investigation for tax evasion, accused of having brought €2 million of untaxed income to a Swiss bank.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-9) He was acquitted in 2016.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-10)

### Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Death")]

Paoli died in [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa") on 24 March 2026, at the age of 91. His last public appearance was at the funeral of Ornella Vanoni the previous November.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto2-7)

**Gino Paoli** (Italian pronunciation:[[ˈdʒiːno ˈpaːoli]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); 23 September 1934 – 24 March 2026) was an Italian singer-songwriter. He wrote a number of songs widely regarded as classics in [Italian popular music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_popular_music "Italian popular music"), including "[Il cielo in una stanza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il_cielo_in_una_stanza_(song) "Il cielo in una stanza (song)")", "Che cosa c'è", "[Senza fine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senza_fine "Senza fine")", "Quattro amici" and "[Sapore di sale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapore_di_sale "Sapore di sale")".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Paoli was born in [Monfalcone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monfalcone "Monfalcone"), near [Trieste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trieste "Trieste"), on 23 September 1934. He moved to [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa") as a child, where he spent all his life.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

After several different jobs, Paoli was signed to [Dischi Ricordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dischi_Ricordi "Dischi Ricordi") with friends and fellow musicians [Luigi Tenco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Tenco "Luigi Tenco") and [Bruno Lauzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Lauzi "Bruno Lauzi"), who would constitute, along with Paoli, [Umberto Bindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umberto_Bindi "Umberto Bindi"), [Giorgio Calabrese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgio_Calabrese "Giorgio Calabrese") and other artists, what is known as the "[Genoese School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoese_School "Genoese School")" of Italian songwriting.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2) His first success was the single "[La gatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_gatta "La gatta")", which has been used in Italian language teaching classes in U.S. middle schools and high schools.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

"[Il cielo in una stanza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il_cielo_in_una_stanza_(song) "Il cielo in una stanza (song)")" was composed in 1959. According to Paoli, the lyrics came to him while lying on a brothel bed. Gazing at the purple ceiling, he thought, "Love can grow at any moment at any place."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-3)[Mina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mina_(Italian_singer) "Mina (Italian singer)")'s single release of the song topped the list of annual sales in Italy[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-4) and reached the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). Video performances of the song were included in the movies _Io bacio... tu baci_ and _[Appuntamento a Ischia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appuntamento\_a\_Ischia "Appuntamento a Ischia")_. It was later featured in _[Goodfellas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas "Goodfellas")_. [Carla Bruni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carla_Bruni "Carla Bruni") covered the song (mixing French with her native Italian) on her debut album _[Quelqu'un m'a dit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quelqu'un\_m'a\_dit "Quelqu'un m'a dit")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Paoli's debut [album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album "Album"), _Gino Paoli_, was released in Italy on 8 October 1961 on Dischi Ricordi.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-5) "Il cielo in una stanza" was followed by "[Sapore di sale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapore_di_sale "Sapore di sale")" (1963), arranged by [Ennio Morricone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ennio_Morricone "Ennio Morricone") and considered to be one of Paoli's most famous songs. In the same year he attempted suicide by shooting himself to the heart (the bullet remained inside his chest).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1974, he returned with the LP _I semafori rossi non sono Dio_, followed by _Il mio mestiere_ (1977). Both showed a more mature inspiration than his 1960s works. In the 1980s, Paoli produced a series of successful albums, and in 1985, he toured Italy together with [Ornella Vanoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornella_Vanoni "Ornella Vanoni").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1987, he [was elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Italian_general_election "1987 Italian general election") to the [Italian Chamber of Deputies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Chamber_of_Deputies "Italian Chamber of Deputies") for the [Italian Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Communist_Party "Italian Communist Party"), soon withdrawing from the party to become a left-wing independent.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-6) He abandoned politics in 1992 to pursue his musical ambitions.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Paoli had several relationships during his lifetime. He first married Anna Fabbri in 1957, with whom he had a son. After separating, he had a long relationship with actress [Stefania Sandrelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefania_Sandrelli "Stefania Sandrelli") in the 1960s; their daughter, [Amanda Sandrelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Sandrelli "Amanda Sandrelli"), is also an actress. He subsequently had an affair with singer [Ornella Vanoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornella_Vanoni "Ornella Vanoni"), who remained a close friend of his throughout their lives. Finally, he began dating Paola Penzo of [Modena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modena "Modena") in the 1970s, marrying her in 1991; the couple had three sons.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto2-7)

### Legal issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Legal issues")]

During an interview in February 2015, when a journalist cited a famous phrase of an Italian minister saying that taxes are a good thing, Paoli insulted him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-8) At the time Paoli was under investigation for tax evasion, accused of having brought €2 million of untaxed income to a Swiss bank.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-9) He was acquitted in 2016.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-10)

### Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Death")]

Paoli died in [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa") on 24 March 2026, at the age of 91. His last public appearance was at the funeral of Ornella Vanoni the previous November.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto2-7)

Married in 1970, Al Bano and Romina Power built a family that would grow alongside their artistic careers, welcoming four children: Ylenia Carrisi, Cristel Carrisi, Romina Carrisi, and Yari Carrisi. The family home in Cellino San Marco became a hub where music, creativity, and familial bonds intertwined, allowing the children to grow in a supportive environment despite their parents’ frequent tours and media obligations. The family’s visibility in Italian media throughout the 1970s and 1980s helped cement their reputation not only as performers but also as a model of multigenerational connection in the public eye.

In the decades that followed, the Carrisi-Power children carried forward their artistic legacy while maintaining close family ties. Ylenia, born in 1970, and the younger siblings all participated in public events, television appearances, and musical projects that reflected both their parents’ influence and their own emerging identities. The family remains closely associated with their Italian heritage, often revisiting the countryside of southern Italy, while also engaging with fans through social media and public celebrations. Posts like this one highlight the enduring importance of unity, love, and shared experience within the Carrisi-Power household, capturing how personal bonds continue to thrive alongside professional achievements. Across more than five decades, the family exemplifies the fusion of artistic legacy, public engagement, and deep-rooted familial connection, remaining a celebrated symbol of love, creativity, and continuity in Italian popular culture.

# Luciano Pavarotti facts: Opera singer's wife, children, career and death explained

24 December 2021, 12:30 | Updated: 19 January 2022, 16:52

![Image 3: Luciano Pavarotti in 1996](https://imgs.smoothradio.com/images/278644?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=pHjxhpJkMsOdl6uc2nWeymuLtAo=)

 Luciano Pavarotti in 1996.  Picture: [Getty](https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/license/1180226370)

[![Image 4: Facebook share](https://www.smoothradio.com/assets_v4r/gusto/img/facebook-share.png)](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?href=www.smoothradio.com%2Fnews%2Fmusic%2Fluciano-pavarotti-facts-wife-children-son-death%2F&app_id=233524320165894)

If there's one person you picture when you think of opera, chances are it's Luciano Pavarotti.

The Italian operatic tenor was one of the few in his genre to successfully crossover into popular music, thanks to his incredible voice and magnetic presence on stage.

Pavarotti was one of the most celebrated tenors of all time, achieving worldwide fame and earning the title 'King of the High Cs'.

*   [**When George Michael and Pavarotti sang a spine-tingling duet of 'Don't Let The Sun Go Down On Me'**](https://www.smoothradio.com/artists/george-michael/pavarotti-duet-dont-let-the-sun-go-down-on-me/)
*   [**When Aretha Franklin had to sing ‘Nessun Dorma’ after Pavarotti fell sick at the Grammys, and it was astonishing**](https://www.smoothradio.com/artists/aretha-franklin/nessun-dorma-pavarotti-grammy-awards-1998-video/)

As one of the Three Tenors, he found a whole new audience when they performed their first concert during the 1990 FIFA World Cup. His most famous performance was that of 'Nessum Dorma', which became his signature song.

Pavarotti sold over 100 million records, with the first Three Tenors recording becoming the best-selling classical album of all time.

He was also known for his charity work on behalf of refugees and the Red Cross, and he often collaborated with many other artists from a variety of genres.

1.   ## Where was Luciano Pavarotti born and what did he look like as a young man?

![Image 5: Pavarotti in 1966](https://imgs.smoothradio.com/images/278647?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=UkgRDH1Ey_yVfqPdNRKxarDWJec=)

 Pavarotti in 1966.  Picture: [Getty](https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/license/143899736)

Luciano Pavarotti was born in 1935 near Modena in Northern Italy.

His parents were Fernando Pavarotti, a baker and amateur tenor, and Adele Venturi, a cigar factory worker.

    *   [**Brian May singing duet with Pavarotti on 'Too Much Love Will Kill You' is spectacular**](https://www.smoothradio.com/artists/queen/brian-may-duet-pavarotti-video-2003/)
    *   [**Watch Bryan Adams sing with Pavarotti in a spine-tingling forgotten duet**](https://www.smoothradio.com/artists/bryan-adams/watch-sing-pavarotti-duet/)

His family were poor, and shared a tiny two-room apartment. Pavarotti later said that his father had a fine tenor voice but rejected a singing career because of nervousness.

![Image 6](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/cWc7vYjgnTs/hqdefault.jpg)

Luciano Pavarotti sings "Nessun dorma" from Turandot (The Three Tenors in Concert 1994)

After abandoning a dream of becoming a football goalkeeper, Pavarotti spent seven years in vocal training. His earliest musical influences were his father's records, including tenors Beniamino Gigli, Giovanni Martinelli, Tito Schipa, and Enrico Caruso.

Pavarotti began studying music in 1954 aged 19 with Arrigo Pola, a respected teacher and professional tenor in Modena.

In 1955, he became a member of the Corale Rossini, a male voice choir from Modena that also included his father, and they won first prize at the International Eisteddfod in Llangollen, Wales.

He later said that this was the most important experience of his life, leading him to pursue a career in music professionally.

2.   ## Who was Luciano Pavarotti's wife?

![Image 7: Luciano Pavarotti with first wife Adua Veroni in 1987](https://imgs.smoothradio.com/images/278652?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=nQKHEMhe8uepG3PZxnQ_i9vsa8I=)

 Luciano Pavarotti with first wife Adua Veroni in 1987.  Picture: [Getty](https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/license/174302916)

Pavarotti was married twice.

He was first married to Adua Veroni from 1961 to 2000.

In December 2003, he married his former personal assistant, Nicoletta Mantovani.

3.   ## How many children did Luciano Pavarotti have?

![Image 8: Luciano Pavarotti with his family (L-R: Cristina Pavarotti, Adua Veroni, Lorenza Pavarotti, Luciano Pavarotti, Giuliana Pavarotti, actress Jacqueline Bisset)](https://imgs.smoothradio.com/images/278649?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=f7Nj6y2sZmv1Yw9_VIGgdB5LmjY=)

 Luciano Pavarotti with his family (L-R: Cristina Pavarotti, Adua Veroni, Lorenza Pavarotti, Luciano Pavarotti, Giuliana Pavarotti, actress Jacqueline Bisset).  Picture: [Getty](https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/license/975339720)

With his first wife Adua, he had three daughters: Lorenza, Cristina, and Giuliana.

He also had another daughter, Alice, with second wife Nicoletta. Alice's twin brother, Riccardo, was stillborn after complications in January 2003.

![Image 9: Luciano Pavarotti poses holding his daughter Alice, with his wife Nicoletta Mantovani](https://imgs.smoothradio.com/images/278650?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=zHS9JfCL26nLJOnmBqJeIVLUdsI=)

 Luciano Pavarotti poses holding his daughter Alice, with his wife Nicoletta Mantovani.  Picture: [Getty](https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/license/158745832)

![Image 10: Daughter Alice with mother Nicoletta in 2021](https://imgs.smoothradio.com/images/278651?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=YIM5s5pf2-vHUQ6cIcnO1qVJu7k=)

 Daughter Alice with mother Nicoletta in 2021.  Picture: [Getty](https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/license/1354936627)

4.   ## What was Pavarotti's cause of death and how old was he?

![Image 11: Luciano Pavarotti in 2006](https://imgs.smoothradio.com/images/278648?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=HyYQelNjzsCdVLIaQTvEnSuskvc=)

 Luciano Pavarotti in 2006.  Picture: [Getty](https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/license/115434025)

While embarking on an international 'farewell tour', Pavarotti was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in July 2006.

He underwent major abdominal surgery, but he died at his home in Modena on September 6, 2007. He was aged 71.

After his death, his manager Terri Robson stated: "The Maestro fought a long, tough battle against the pancreatic cancer which eventually took his life. In fitting with the approach that characterised his life and work, he remained positive until finally succumbing to the last stages of his illness".

Pavarotti's funeral was held at Modena Cathedral. Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Kofi Annan were in attendance, while the Frecce Tricolori, the aerobatic demonstration team of the Italian Air Force, flew overhead.

# Luciano Pavarotti facts: Opera singer's wife, children, career and death explained

24 December 2021, 12:30 | Updated: 19 January 2022, 16:52

![Image 3: Luciano Pavarotti in 1996](https://imgs.smoothradio.com/images/278644?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=pHjxhpJkMsOdl6uc2nWeymuLtAo=)

 Luciano Pavarotti in 1996.  Picture: [Getty](https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/license/1180226370)

[![Image 4: Facebook share](https://www.smoothradio.com/assets_v4r/gusto/img/facebook-share.png)](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?href=www.smoothradio.com%2Fnews%2Fmusic%2Fluciano-pavarotti-facts-wife-children-son-death%2F&app_id=233524320165894)

If there's one person you picture when you think of opera, chances are it's Luciano Pavarotti.

The Italian operatic tenor was one of the few in his genre to successfully crossover into popular music, thanks to his incredible voice and magnetic presence on stage.

Pavarotti was one of the most celebrated tenors of all time, achieving worldwide fame and earning the title 'King of the High Cs'.

*   [**When George Michael and Pavarotti sang a spine-tingling duet of 'Don't Let The Sun Go Down On Me'**](https://www.smoothradio.com/artists/george-michael/pavarotti-duet-dont-let-the-sun-go-down-on-me/)
*   [**When Aretha Franklin had to sing ‘Nessun Dorma’ after Pavarotti fell sick at the Grammys, and it was astonishing**](https://www.smoothradio.com/artists/aretha-franklin/nessun-dorma-pavarotti-grammy-awards-1998-video/)

As one of the Three Tenors, he found a whole new audience when they performed their first concert during the 1990 FIFA World Cup. His most famous performance was that of 'Nessum Dorma', which became his signature song.

Pavarotti sold over 100 million records, with the first Three Tenors recording becoming the best-selling classical album of all time.

He was also known for his charity work on behalf of refugees and the Red Cross, and he often collaborated with many other artists from a variety of genres.

1.   ## Where was Luciano Pavarotti born and what did he look like as a young man?

![Image 5: Pavarotti in 1966](https://imgs.smoothradio.com/images/278647?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=UkgRDH1Ey_yVfqPdNRKxarDWJec=)

 Pavarotti in 1966.  Picture: [Getty](https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/license/143899736)

Luciano Pavarotti was born in 1935 near Modena in Northern Italy.

His parents were Fernando Pavarotti, a baker and amateur tenor, and Adele Venturi, a cigar factory worker.

    *   [**Brian May singing duet with Pavarotti on 'Too Much Love Will Kill You' is spectacular**](https://www.smoothradio.com/artists/queen/brian-may-duet-pavarotti-video-2003/)
    *   [**Watch Bryan Adams sing with Pavarotti in a spine-tingling forgotten duet**](https://www.smoothradio.com/artists/bryan-adams/watch-sing-pavarotti-duet/)

His family were poor, and shared a tiny two-room apartment. Pavarotti later said that his father had a fine tenor voice but rejected a singing career because of nervousness.

![Image 6](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/cWc7vYjgnTs/hqdefault.jpg)

Luciano Pavarotti sings "Nessun dorma" from Turandot (The Three Tenors in Concert 1994)

After abandoning a dream of becoming a football goalkeeper, Pavarotti spent seven years in vocal training. His earliest musical influences were his father's records, including tenors Beniamino Gigli, Giovanni Martinelli, Tito Schipa, and Enrico Caruso.

Pavarotti began studying music in 1954 aged 19 with Arrigo Pola, a respected teacher and professional tenor in Modena.

In 1955, he became a member of the Corale Rossini, a male voice choir from Modena that also included his father, and they won first prize at the International Eisteddfod in Llangollen, Wales.

He later said that this was the most important experience of his life, leading him to pursue a career in music professionally.

![Image 7: Luciano Pavarotti with first wife Adua Veroni in 1987](https://imgs.smoothradio.com/images/278652?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=nQKHEMhe8uepG3PZxnQ_i9vsa8I=)

 Luciano Pavarotti with first wife Adua Veroni in 1987.  Picture: [Getty](https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/license/174302916)

He was first married to Adua Veroni from 1961 to 2000.

In December 2003, he married his former personal assistant, Nicoletta Mantovani.

![Image 8: Luciano Pavarotti with his family (L-R: Cristina Pavarotti, Adua Veroni, Lorenza Pavarotti, Luciano Pavarotti, Giuliana Pavarotti, actress Jacqueline Bisset)](https://imgs.smoothradio.com/images/278649?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=f7Nj6y2sZmv1Yw9_VIGgdB5LmjY=)

With his first wife Adua, he had three daughters: Lorenza, Cristina, and Giuliana.

He also had another daughter, Alice, with second wife Nicoletta. Alice's twin brother, Riccardo, was stillborn after complications in January 2003.

4.   ## What was Pavarotti's cause of death and how old was he?

![Image 11: Luciano Pavarotti in 2006](https://imgs.smoothradio.com/images/278648?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=HyYQelNjzsCdVLIaQTvEnSuskvc=)

 Luciano Pavarotti in 2006.  Picture: [Getty](https://www.gettyimages.co.uk/license/115434025)

While embarking on an international 'farewell tour', Pavarotti was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in July 2006.

He underwent major abdominal surgery, but he died at his home in Modena on September 6, 2007. He was aged 71.

After his death, his manager Terri Robson stated: "The Maestro fought a long, tough battle against the pancreatic cancer which eventually took his life. In fitting with the approach that characterised his life and work, he remained positive until finally succumbing to the last stages of his illness".

Pavarotti's funeral was held at Modena Cathedral. Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Kofi Annan were in attendance, while the Frecce Tricolori, the aerobatic demonstration team of the Italian Air Force, flew overhead.

# A family of five was living off-grid in a remote cabin in central Italy. Then the courts intervened

By Barbie Latza Nadeau

Updated Nov 23, 2025

Updated Nov 23, 2025, 11:18 AM ET

PUBLISHED Nov 23, 2025, 11:08 AM ET

Facebook Tweet[Email](mailto:?subject=CNN%20content%20share&body=Check%20out%20this%20article%3A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.cnn.com%2F2025%2F11%2F23%2Feurope%2Fbimbi-nel-bosco-italy-courts-intl "Share with email")Link Threads

![Image 1: Nathan Trevallion and Catherine Birmingham pose for a picture with their children, who have been removed from their custody following an order from a juvenile court. A portion of this photo has been blurred by CNN to protect identities.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/img-3302-1-blur.jpg?c=original&q=w_860,c_fill)

Nathan Trevallion and Catherine Birmingham pose for a picture with their children, who have been removed from their custody following an order from a juvenile court. A portion of this photo has been blurred by CNN to protect identities.

Courtesy Catherine Birmingham

The self-described idyllic life of a family of five living in an Italian forest with horses, donkeys and chickens has stalled after a court ordered the children be removed and placed in foster care.

Patrol cars were dispatched to remove the children from their home in Abruzzo to a church-run care facility. The mother is staying at the same premise but the parents have limited access to the children, their family lawyer said.

The fate of the children, known in Italian as the _Bimbi nel Bosc_ o or kids in the woods, has captivated the country. Tens of thousands of people have signed an online petition to reunite the family.

Ad Feedback

The parents, Nathan Trevallion, a 51-year-old British former professional chef, and Catherine Birmingham, a 45-year-old Australian life coach and former equestrian trainer, were named in an order issued by a L’Aquila court as parents of the children – one eight-year-old and six-year-old twins.

“The family unit lives in housing hardship as the building has not been declared habitable,” the order states. “The members of the Trevallion family have no social interaction, no fixed income, the home has no toilet facilities, and the children do not attend school. The order is based on the risk of violating the right to social life in consideration of the serious and harmful violations of the children’s rights to physical and mental integrity the parents should be suspended from parental responsibility.”

Giovanni Angelucci, the family’s lawyer, says the family heats the home with fireplaces and uses solar panels for light and to charge their devices. The family removed running water to avoid microplastics as well as costs and instead draws fresh water from a well on the property. They don’t have an indoor toilet but instead use an outdoor composting toilet.

![Image 2: Nathan Trevallion and Catherine Birmingham pose for a picture with their children. A portion of this photo has been blurred by CNN to protect identities.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/image-blur.jpg?c=original&q=w_780,c_fill)

Nathan Trevallion and Catherine Birmingham pose for a picture with their children. A portion of this photo has been blurred by CNN to protect identities.

Courtesy Catherine Birmingham

![Image 3: Photos from the Catherine Birmingham's website show parts of the property in Abruzzo, Italy.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/img-4945-1.jpg?c=original&q=w_780,c_fill)

Photos from the Catherine Birmingham's website show parts of the property in Abruzzo, Italy.

Courtesy Catherine Birmingham

The family’s living situation came to light in September 2024 after all five were hospitalized for poisoning after eating wild mushrooms from the forest. After that time, the family was visited by social service officials and law enforcement, but their lawyer said they did not comply with recommendations to have the children receive regular medical care and attend schools.

Trevallion told local media at the time he was shocked by the decision. “They are happy, smell good, well-mannered, and well-fed; why break this bond?” he said Friday, according to La Repubblica newspaper. CNN reached out to the family via Birmingham’s website, which advises that they don’t check electronic communications often.

Angelluci said the family will appeal the decision next week.

Birmingham runs a life coaching and energy reading business, according to [her website,](https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcatherinelouisebirmingham.com%2F&data=05%7C02%7CJedd.Rosche%40cnn.com%7C820c15ee70f64bec89d008de2aa50ae3%7C0eb48825e8714459bc72d0ecd68f1f39%7C0%7C0%7C638995085512461412%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=HpsFZCFX3mU0w47ufJnX27O2VB5EW9pFRnwAA6Nswl8%3D&reserved=0) which is filled with images of animals and the children – photos the court order said violated the children’s privacy and were posted only to show the appearance of a normal living situation after the social services’ investigation began.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and her deputy Matteo Salvini have both criticized the court decision. Meloni, who said the removal of the children was “alarming,” has called the Italian Justice Minister Carlo Nordio over the case, according to her spokesman.

Salvini, who plans to visit the family home next week, told reporters at the Venice Bienniele on Friday that it was “shameful that the State is concerned with private education and the personal life choices of two parents who found Italy a hospitable country, yet it steals their children.”

![Image 4: Nathan Trevallion and Catherine Birmingham pose for a picture with their children. A portion of this photo has been blurred by CNN to protect identities.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/d0ee1b08-6af5-4473-9ad9-c250866664ff-1-blur.jpg?c=original&q=w_860,c_fill)

The family purchased the home in 2021, at which time Birmingham wrote on her website, “Recently we found our dream forever home. … With the energy of the place being very special, we bring people to stay for healing and awakening, connecting to the wild, without and within, eating home grown and home cooked organic vegan food.”

Giuseppe Masciulli, the mayor of nearby Palmoli, also condemned the removal of the children. “I’m a father myself, so I was deeply shocked by the situation,” he told CNN, adding that he believed the situation could be resolved if the family promises to meet certain requirements, including reinstalling running water and meeting with the local school on a weekly basis to assess the children’s academic progress.

# A family of five was living off-grid in a remote cabin in central Italy. Then the courts intervened

By Barbie Latza Nadeau

Updated Nov 23, 2025

Updated Nov 23, 2025, 11:18 AM ET

PUBLISHED Nov 23, 2025, 11:08 AM ET

Facebook Tweet[Email](mailto:?subject=CNN%20content%20share&body=Check%20out%20this%20article%3A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.cnn.com%2F2025%2F11%2F23%2Feurope%2Fbimbi-nel-bosco-italy-courts-intl "Share with email")Link Threads

![Image 1: Nathan Trevallion and Catherine Birmingham pose for a picture with their children, who have been removed from their custody following an order from a juvenile court. A portion of this photo has been blurred by CNN to protect identities.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/img-3302-1-blur.jpg?c=original&q=w_860,c_fill)

Nathan Trevallion and Catherine Birmingham pose for a picture with their children, who have been removed from their custody following an order from a juvenile court. A portion of this photo has been blurred by CNN to protect identities.

Courtesy Catherine Birmingham

The self-described idyllic life of a family of five living in an Italian forest with horses, donkeys and chickens has stalled after a court ordered the children be removed and placed in foster care.

Patrol cars were dispatched to remove the children from their home in Abruzzo to a church-run care facility. The mother is staying at the same premise but the parents have limited access to the children, their family lawyer said.

The fate of the children, known in Italian as the _Bimbi nel Bosc_ o or kids in the woods, has captivated the country. Tens of thousands of people have signed an online petition to reunite the family.

Ad Feedback

The parents, Nathan Trevallion, a 51-year-old British former professional chef, and Catherine Birmingham, a 45-year-old Australian life coach and former equestrian trainer, were named in an order issued by a L’Aquila court as parents of the children – one eight-year-old and six-year-old twins.

“The family unit lives in housing hardship as the building has not been declared habitable,” the order states. “The members of the Trevallion family have no social interaction, no fixed income, the home has no toilet facilities, and the children do not attend school. The order is based on the risk of violating the right to social life in consideration of the serious and harmful violations of the children’s rights to physical and mental integrity the parents should be suspended from parental responsibility.”

Giovanni Angelucci, the family’s lawyer, says the family heats the home with fireplaces and uses solar panels for light and to charge their devices. The family removed running water to avoid microplastics as well as costs and instead draws fresh water from a well on the property. They don’t have an indoor toilet but instead use an outdoor composting toilet.

![Image 2: Nathan Trevallion and Catherine Birmingham pose for a picture with their children. A portion of this photo has been blurred by CNN to protect identities.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/image-blur.jpg?c=original&q=w_780,c_fill)

Nathan Trevallion and Catherine Birmingham pose for a picture with their children. A portion of this photo has been blurred by CNN to protect identities.

Courtesy Catherine Birmingham

![Image 3: Photos from the Catherine Birmingham's website show parts of the property in Abruzzo, Italy.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/img-4945-1.jpg?c=original&q=w_780,c_fill)

Photos from the Catherine Birmingham's website show parts of the property in Abruzzo, Italy.

Courtesy Catherine Birmingham

The family’s living situation came to light in September 2024 after all five were hospitalized for poisoning after eating wild mushrooms from the forest. After that time, the family was visited by social service officials and law enforcement, but their lawyer said they did not comply with recommendations to have the children receive regular medical care and attend schools.

Trevallion told local media at the time he was shocked by the decision. “They are happy, smell good, well-mannered, and well-fed; why break this bond?” he said Friday, according to La Repubblica newspaper. CNN reached out to the family via Birmingham’s website, which advises that they don’t check electronic communications often.

Angelluci said the family will appeal the decision next week.

Birmingham runs a life coaching and energy reading business, according to [her website,](https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcatherinelouisebirmingham.com%2F&data=05%7C02%7CJedd.Rosche%40cnn.com%7C820c15ee70f64bec89d008de2aa50ae3%7C0eb48825e8714459bc72d0ecd68f1f39%7C0%7C0%7C638995085512461412%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=HpsFZCFX3mU0w47ufJnX27O2VB5EW9pFRnwAA6Nswl8%3D&reserved=0) which is filled with images of animals and the children – photos the court order said violated the children’s privacy and were posted only to show the appearance of a normal living situation after the social services’ investigation began.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and her deputy Matteo Salvini have both criticized the court decision. Meloni, who said the removal of the children was “alarming,” has called the Italian Justice Minister Carlo Nordio over the case, according to her spokesman.

Salvini, who plans to visit the family home next week, told reporters at the Venice Bienniele on Friday that it was “shameful that the State is concerned with private education and the personal life choices of two parents who found Italy a hospitable country, yet it steals their children.”

![Image 4: Nathan Trevallion and Catherine Birmingham pose for a picture with their children. A portion of this photo has been blurred by CNN to protect identities.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/d0ee1b08-6af5-4473-9ad9-c250866664ff-1-blur.jpg?c=original&q=w_860,c_fill)

Nathan Trevallion and Catherine Birmingham pose for a picture with their children. A portion of this photo has been blurred by CNN to protect identities.

Courtesy Catherine Birmingham

The family purchased the home in 2021, at which time Birmingham wrote on her website, “Recently we found our dream forever home. … With the energy of the place being very special, we bring people to stay for healing and awakening, connecting to the wild, without and within, eating home grown and home cooked organic vegan food.”

Giuseppe Masciulli, the mayor of nearby Palmoli, also condemned the removal of the children. “I’m a father myself, so I was deeply shocked by the situation,” he told CNN, adding that he believed the situation could be resolved if the family promises to meet certain requirements, including reinstalling running water and meeting with the local school on a weekly basis to assess the children’s academic progress.

# Andrea Bocelli facts: wife, famous songs, family and everything to know about the Italian tenor

7 March 2023, 09:12 | Updated: 30 January 2024, 12:19

![Image 3](https://cf-images.eu-west-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6057949401001/5e5d23f7-3894-4407-b840-eddb3e679d5f/fcc6bcb7-aaac-462f-ab95-f4c46aa06050/640x360/match/image.jpg)

Andrea Bocelli - ‘Nessun Dorma’ (live at The Global Awards 2018)

![Image 4: Classic FM](https://imgs.classicfm.com/images/273255?crop=1_1&width=200&format=webp&signature=UETG6EsE_Hl54V2b0IhTa2WzwcM=)
By Classic FM

[@ClassicFM](https://x.com/ClassicFM "Follow Classic FM on X")

[![Image 5: Facebook share](https://www.classicfm.com/assets_v4r/gusto/img/facebook-share.png)](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?href=www.classicfm.com%2Fartists%2Fandrea-bocelli%2Fwife-blind-songs-children-facts%2F&app_id=357357177653391)

The world’s most popular living tenor and a best-selling classical crossover artist – Andrea Bocelli is one of the finest artists of our generation. But how much do you know about the great Italian singer?

Operatic tenor [Andrea Bocelli](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/) is one of classical music’s biggest-selling living artists. The beloved Italian singer, best known for his crossover hit ‘[Time to Say Goodbye](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/time-to-say-goodbye-translation/)’ with Sarah Brightman, has recorded everything from popular Neapolitan songs, to complete operas.

From his best-known songs, to his wife and [children](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/children-matteo-amos-virginia-age/), to his age, find out all you need to know about this legendary tenor.

**Read more:**[**Who are Andrea Bocelli’s children and what do they do?**](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/children-matteo-amos-virginia-age/)

1.   ## How old is Andrea Bocelli?

Andrea Angel Bocelli was born on 22 September 1958 in Laiatico, Pisa in the Italian region of Tuscany. In September 2022, he turned 64 years old.

**Read more:**[**Andrea Bocelli’s lockdown concert becomes biggest classical live stream in YouTube history**](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/concert-empty-milan-duomo-cathedral-world-record/)

![Image 6: Andrea Bocelli pictured at two years old (1960)](https://imgs.classicfm.com/images/309907?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=HX21Iey8N7eAZJpgHCV334ubdww=)

 Andrea Bocelli pictured at two years old (1960).  Picture: Alamy 

2.   ## Is Andrea Bocelli blind?

Andrea Bocelli lost his sight after a football accident when he was just 12 years old. The singer had already experienced problems with his eyes, and was diagnosed with glaucoma at an early age.

**Read more:**[**Is Andrea Bocelli blind? The story behind the famed tenor’s sight loss**](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/blind-reason-sight-loss/)

![Image 7: Andrea Bocelli lost his sight after a football accident when he was 12 years old](https://imgs.classicfm.com/images/309906?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=t0j-K7WECBdrYuL85f-R8GsOtsk=)

 Andrea Bocelli lost his sight after a football accident when he was 12 years old.  Picture: Alamy 

3.   ## Who is Andrea Bocelli’s wife?

Andrea Bocelli married his wife and manager Veronica Berti, in a [stylish ceremony in Tuscany](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/marriage-veronica-berti-wedding-italy/) in 2014. Two years before their marriage, in 2012 Veronica gave birth to the couple’s first child Virginia – Bocelli’s third child, but first daughter.

**Read more:**[**Andrea Bocelli sings ‘Hallelujah’ with his eight-year-old daughter in magical duet**](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/virginia-daughter-hallelujah-duet-christmas-concert/)

![Image 8: Andrea Bocelli and Veronica Berti leave the Sanctuary of Madonna di Montenero after their wedding on March 21, 2014 i](https://imgs.classicfm.com/images/309914?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=kSJeW9gQh_88ocJT3j-6CfDzVwE=)

 Andrea Bocelli and Veronica Berti leave the Sanctuary of Madonna di Montenero after their wedding on March 21, 2014 i.  Picture: Getty 

4.   ## Who are Andrea Bocelli’s children, and who was his first wife?

The Italian singer has two children from his first marriage to Enrica Cenzatti, and one from his second.

Amos, his first son with Enrica, was born on 22 February 1995. Their second son, [Matteo](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/son-matteo-bocelli-facts/), was born on 8 October 1997. Both sons are musical; Amos has played piano alongside his father in various TV appearances, while Matteo has released a number of duets with him, including the hit ‘[Fall on Me](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/son-matteo-perform-stunning-fall-on-me-duet/)’ which appeared in Disney’s _The Nutcracker and The Four Realms_.

Speaking to _Billboard_ about the difference between his and Matteo’s voices, Andrea said: “Technically they are very different, but there is one thing that makes them most similar: the attitude.”

Bocelli’s youngest, Virginia, turned 10 years old in 2022. She is also musical, singing ‘[Hallelujah](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/virginia-daughter-hallelujah-duet-christmas-concert/)’ and ‘[Ich Liebe Dich](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/ich-liebe-dich-duet-daughter-virginia/)’ in videos with her father that have proved very popular with fans.

![Image 9](https://cf-images.eu-west-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/jit/6057949401001/b03eda54-88de-49d8-939c-8f4c89a3eefd/main/640x360/30s16ms/match/image.jpg)Andrea & Matteo Bocelli- Fall On Me   
5.   ## Where does Andrea Bocelli live?

Bocelli lives in a former hotel in the charming town of Forte dei Marmi in Tuscany, with his wife and daughter.

**Read more:**[**Where does Andrea Bocelli live? Behind the scenes in his Italian family home**](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/pictures/home-family/)

![Image 10: Andrea Bocelli's house in Forte dei Marmi, Tuscany](https://imgs.classicfm.com/images/309925?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=ejOQOnapIVkswLezISTK5vJ4kEA=)

 Andrea Bocelli's house in Forte dei Marmi, Tuscany.  Picture: Classic FM 

6.   ## How did Andrea Bocelli become famous?

Despite the setback with his sight, the young Andrea showed huge potential as a singer, winning his first competition aged just 14 with a rendition of the Neapolitan song ‘[O Sole Mio](https://www.classicfm.com/discover-music/o-sole-mio-lyrics/)’. However, it didn’t seem that music was quite the right career choice for Bocelli – he went to the University of Pisa to study law, but kept singing in bars for extra money.

Then, Bocelli’s luck changed when a demo tape of him singing found its way into the hands of [Luciano Pavarotti](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/luciano-pavarotti/), via the Italian rock star Zucchero. Bocelli was invited on tour with Zucchero, where the two performed the song ‘Miserere’ together. Pavarotti remained supportive of Bocelli in the early days of his career, inviting him to perform at his annual charity gala concert in Modena, Pavarotti & Friends.

![Image 11: Luciano Pavarotti perfoms with Andrea Bocelli at the 'Pavarotti & Friends' 2003 concert in Modena](https://imgs.classicfm.com/images/309926?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=-h_SRXKTEi9zkqN-XyRbrHsZRko=)

 Luciano Pavarotti perfoms with Andrea Bocelli at the 'Pavarotti & Friends' 2003 concert in Modena.  Picture: Alamy 

7.   ## What is Andrea Bocelli’s most famous song?

Andrea’s massive-selling duet with Sarah Brightman, ‘Time To Say Goodbye’, was originally intended as a farewell song to boxer Henry Maske (who was friends with Brightman), and was first performed at his final fight in 1996.

It has become one of the most successful singles in history, breaking records across the world and becoming Bocelli’s signature song, as both a solo and duet.

‘The Prayer’, a duet Bocelli recorded with Celine Dion in 1999, and Puccini’s glorious tenor aria ‘Nessun dorma’, have also become melodies closely associated with Bocelli. The tenor most recently sang the aria at The Queen’s [Platinum Jubilee](https://www.classicfm.com/music-news/videos/prince-william-conducts-orchestra-platinum-jubilee/) concert.

**Read more:**[**Andrea Bocelli’s greatest ever songs**](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/andrea-bocelli-greatest-songs/)

8.   ## Who are Andrea Bocelli’s parents?

Andrea Bocelli was born the son of Alessandro and Edi Bocelli. His family lived on a farm, selling farm machinery and making wine for a living.

Along with his brother, Alberto, Andrea now has his very own brand of wine. Made from grapes grown on his family farm, the ‘Bocelli Family’ label has already wowed wine critics and earned the Bocellis the respect of the wine-making world.

![Image 13: Andrea Bocelli and his brother Alberto, pictured on the family’s wine estate in Lajatico, Pisa](https://imgs.classicfm.com/images/309931?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=yP4FXAAZyIOj2i0JksiXDxPU48I=)

 Andrea Bocelli and his brother Alberto, pictured on the family’s wine estate in Lajatico, Pisa.  Picture: Alamy 

9.   ## What is Andrea Bocelli’s vocal range?

Andrea Bocelli is a tenor, whose range is estimated to span from around C sharp 2, up to D5.

His stylistic range spans from crossover pop hits, to complete operas. In 1998, Bocelli took to the dramatic stage for the first time when he played the role of Rodolfo in Puccini’s _La bohème,_ at the Teatro Comunale in Cagliari. He has also sung Puccini’s _Madam Butterfly_ and _Tosca,_ and Verdi’s _Requiem,_ live.

![Image 14](https://cf-images.eu-west-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/jit/6057949401001/03881019-1b11-40c5-aa07-cbcffefdff9b/main/640x360/48s379ms/match/image.jpg)Andrea Bocelli and Joseph Calleja duet in Malta   
10.   ## Andrea Bocelli’s albums: what was his debut, and his latest, album?

Bocelli’s debut album, _Il mare calmo della sera_(1994) was a classical crossover album which included Puccini’s great aria ‘E lucevan le stelle’.

The star tenor has released 17 albums in total, most recently _Believe_, which came out in November 2020. It features a duet with Alison Krauss and a previously unheard track by the late film great, [Ennio Morricone](https://www.classicfm.com/composers/morricone/).

In October 2022, the tenor released a [Christmas album](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/voice-change-christmas-family-interview/) with his son Matteo, and daughter Virginia. _A Family Christmas_ features trio arrangements of traditional carols and new compositions specially written for the family.

# Andrea Bocelli facts: wife, famous songs, family and everything to know about the Italian tenor

7 March 2023, 09:12 | Updated: 30 January 2024, 12:19

![Image 3](https://cf-images.eu-west-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6057949401001/5e5d23f7-3894-4407-b840-eddb3e679d5f/fcc6bcb7-aaac-462f-ab95-f4c46aa06050/640x360/match/image.jpg)

The world’s most popular living tenor and a best-selling classical crossover artist – Andrea Bocelli is one of the finest artists of our generation. But how much do you know about the great Italian singer?

Operatic tenor [Andrea Bocelli](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/) is one of classical music’s biggest-selling living artists. The beloved Italian singer, best known for his crossover hit ‘[Time to Say Goodbye](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/time-to-say-goodbye-translation/)’ with Sarah Brightman, has recorded everything from popular Neapolitan songs, to complete operas.

From his best-known songs, to his wife and [children](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/children-matteo-amos-virginia-age/), to his age, find out all you need to know about this legendary tenor.

**Read more:**[**Who are Andrea Bocelli’s children and what do they do?**](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/children-matteo-amos-virginia-age/)

1.   ## How old is Andrea Bocelli?

Andrea Angel Bocelli was born on 22 September 1958 in Laiatico, Pisa in the Italian region of Tuscany. In September 2022, he turned 64 years old.

**Read more:**[**Andrea Bocelli’s lockdown concert becomes biggest classical live stream in YouTube history**](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/concert-empty-milan-duomo-cathedral-world-record/)

 Andrea Bocelli pictured at two years old (1960).  Picture: Alamy 

2.   ## Is Andrea Bocelli blind?

Andrea Bocelli lost his sight after a football accident when he was just 12 years old. The singer had already experienced problems with his eyes, and was diagnosed with glaucoma at an early age.

**Read more:**[**Is Andrea Bocelli blind? The story behind the famed tenor’s sight loss**](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/blind-reason-sight-loss/)

![Image 7: Andrea Bocelli lost his sight after a football accident when he was 12 years old](https://imgs.classicfm.com/images/309906?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=t0j-K7WECBdrYuL85f-R8GsOtsk=)

 Andrea Bocelli lost his sight after a football accident when he was 12 years old.  Picture: Alamy 

3.   ## Who is Andrea Bocelli’s wife?

Andrea Bocelli married his wife and manager Veronica Berti, in a [stylish ceremony in Tuscany](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/marriage-veronica-berti-wedding-italy/) in 2014. Two years before their marriage, in 2012 Veronica gave birth to the couple’s first child Virginia – Bocelli’s third child, but first daughter.

**Read more:**[**Andrea Bocelli sings ‘Hallelujah’ with his eight-year-old daughter in magical duet**](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/virginia-daughter-hallelujah-duet-christmas-concert/)

![Image 8: Andrea Bocelli and Veronica Berti leave the Sanctuary of Madonna di Montenero after their wedding on March 21, 2014 i](https://imgs.classicfm.com/images/309914?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=kSJeW9gQh_88ocJT3j-6CfDzVwE=)

 Andrea Bocelli and Veronica Berti leave the Sanctuary of Madonna di Montenero after their wedding on March 21, 2014 i.  Picture: Getty 

4.   ## Who are Andrea Bocelli’s children, and who was his first wife?

The Italian singer has two children from his first marriage to Enrica Cenzatti, and one from his second.

Amos, his first son with Enrica, was born on 22 February 1995. Their second son, [Matteo](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/son-matteo-bocelli-facts/), was born on 8 October 1997. Both sons are musical; Amos has played piano alongside his father in various TV appearances, while Matteo has released a number of duets with him, including the hit ‘[Fall on Me](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/son-matteo-perform-stunning-fall-on-me-duet/)’ which appeared in Disney’s _The Nutcracker and The Four Realms_.

Speaking to _Billboard_ about the difference between his and Matteo’s voices, Andrea said: “Technically they are very different, but there is one thing that makes them most similar: the attitude.”

Bocelli’s youngest, Virginia, turned 10 years old in 2022. She is also musical, singing ‘[Hallelujah](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/virginia-daughter-hallelujah-duet-christmas-concert/)’ and ‘[Ich Liebe Dich](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/ich-liebe-dich-duet-daughter-virginia/)’ in videos with her father that have proved very popular with fans.

5.   ## Where does Andrea Bocelli live?

Bocelli lives in a former hotel in the charming town of Forte dei Marmi in Tuscany, with his wife and daughter.

 Andrea Bocelli's house in Forte dei Marmi, Tuscany.  Picture: Classic FM 

6.   ## How did Andrea Bocelli become famous?

Despite the setback with his sight, the young Andrea showed huge potential as a singer, winning his first competition aged just 14 with a rendition of the Neapolitan song ‘[O Sole Mio](https://www.classicfm.com/discover-music/o-sole-mio-lyrics/)’. However, it didn’t seem that music was quite the right career choice for Bocelli – he went to the University of Pisa to study law, but kept singing in bars for extra money.

Then, Bocelli’s luck changed when a demo tape of him singing found its way into the hands of [Luciano Pavarotti](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/luciano-pavarotti/), via the Italian rock star Zucchero. Bocelli was invited on tour with Zucchero, where the two performed the song ‘Miserere’ together. Pavarotti remained supportive of Bocelli in the early days of his career, inviting him to perform at his annual charity gala concert in Modena, Pavarotti & Friends.

![Image 11: Luciano Pavarotti perfoms with Andrea Bocelli at the 'Pavarotti & Friends' 2003 concert in Modena](https://imgs.classicfm.com/images/309926?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=-h_SRXKTEi9zkqN-XyRbrHsZRko=)

 Luciano Pavarotti perfoms with Andrea Bocelli at the 'Pavarotti & Friends' 2003 concert in Modena.  Picture: Alamy 

7.   ## What is Andrea Bocelli’s most famous song?

Andrea’s massive-selling duet with Sarah Brightman, ‘Time To Say Goodbye’, was originally intended as a farewell song to boxer Henry Maske (who was friends with Brightman), and was first performed at his final fight in 1996.

It has become one of the most successful singles in history, breaking records across the world and becoming Bocelli’s signature song, as both a solo and duet.

‘The Prayer’, a duet Bocelli recorded with Celine Dion in 1999, and Puccini’s glorious tenor aria ‘Nessun dorma’, have also become melodies closely associated with Bocelli. The tenor most recently sang the aria at The Queen’s [Platinum Jubilee](https://www.classicfm.com/music-news/videos/prince-william-conducts-orchestra-platinum-jubilee/) concert.

**Read more:**[**Andrea Bocelli’s greatest ever songs**](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/andrea-bocelli-greatest-songs/)

![Image 12](https://cf-images.eu-west-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/static/6057949401001/36579de8-718e-46dc-ad67-9732a0190146/eb3d3829-a69d-4b1a-a4f8-e49a473064de/640x360/match/image.jpg)Andrea Bocelli sings ‘Time To Say Goodbye’ (live at The Global Awards 2018)   
8.   ## Who are Andrea Bocelli’s parents?

Andrea Bocelli was born the son of Alessandro and Edi Bocelli. His family lived on a farm, selling farm machinery and making wine for a living.

Along with his brother, Alberto, Andrea now has his very own brand of wine. Made from grapes grown on his family farm, the ‘Bocelli Family’ label has already wowed wine critics and earned the Bocellis the respect of the wine-making world.

![Image 13: Andrea Bocelli and his brother Alberto, pictured on the family’s wine estate in Lajatico, Pisa](https://imgs.classicfm.com/images/309931?crop=16_9&width=660&relax=1&format=webp&signature=yP4FXAAZyIOj2i0JksiXDxPU48I=)

 Andrea Bocelli and his brother Alberto, pictured on the family’s wine estate in Lajatico, Pisa.  Picture: Alamy 

9.   ## What is Andrea Bocelli’s vocal range?

Andrea Bocelli is a tenor, whose range is estimated to span from around C sharp 2, up to D5.

His stylistic range spans from crossover pop hits, to complete operas. In 1998, Bocelli took to the dramatic stage for the first time when he played the role of Rodolfo in Puccini’s _La bohème,_ at the Teatro Comunale in Cagliari. He has also sung Puccini’s _Madam Butterfly_ and _Tosca,_ and Verdi’s _Requiem,_ live.

![Image 14](https://cf-images.eu-west-1.prod.boltdns.net/v1/jit/6057949401001/03881019-1b11-40c5-aa07-cbcffefdff9b/main/640x360/48s379ms/match/image.jpg)Andrea Bocelli and Joseph Calleja duet in Malta   
10.   ## Andrea Bocelli’s albums: what was his debut, and his latest, album?

Bocelli’s debut album, _Il mare calmo della sera_(1994) was a classical crossover album which included Puccini’s great aria ‘E lucevan le stelle’.

The star tenor has released 17 albums in total, most recently _Believe_, which came out in November 2020. It features a duet with Alison Krauss and a previously unheard track by the late film great, [Ennio Morricone](https://www.classicfm.com/composers/morricone/).

In October 2022, the tenor released a [Christmas album](https://www.classicfm.com/artists/andrea-bocelli/voice-change-christmas-family-interview/) with his son Matteo, and daughter Virginia. _A Family Christmas_ features trio arrangements of traditional carols and new compositions specially written for the family.

Ornella Vanoni, the revered [Italian](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/italian) singer whose illustrious seven-decade career captivated audiences worldwide with hits such as "Senza Fine" and "L’appuntamento," has died at the age of 91.

[Italian](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/italian) Prime Minister [Giorgia Meloni](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/giorgia-meloni) expressed profound sorrow following the news, stating on X that Vanoni’s "unmistakable voice" had left an indelible mark on Italian culture for generations.

"Italy loses a unique artist who leaves us with an unrepeatable artistic heritage," Meloni remarked.

[_La Stampa_](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/la-stampa) reported that Vanoni passed away from cardiac arrest at her home in [Milan](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/milan).

Known affectionately as "The Lady of Italian Song," Vanoni’s prolific career saw her record over 100 albums, selling more than 55 million copies and cementing her iconic status across multiple generations of fans, according to LaPresse newspaper.

Born in [Milan](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/milan) in 1937, Vanoni initially pursued a passion for theatre, culminating in performances on [Broadway](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/broadway) in 1964.

![Image 3: American actor Rock Hudson hands the "Golden Record" to Italian singer Ornella Vanoni, at a ceremony in the Piccolo Teatro](https://static.the-independent.com/2025/11/22/12/Italy_Ornella_Vanoni_66686.jpg)

open image in gallery

American actor Rock Hudson hands the "Golden Record" to Italian singer Ornella Vanoni, at a ceremony in the Piccolo Teatro(Copyright 1969 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.)

However, her distinctive musical talent, characterised by what _LaPresse_ described as a "highly personal and sophisticated performing style" and a vast repertoire spanning jazz to pop, led her to collaborate with some of Italy’s and the world’s most significant songwriters.

Her partnership and romantic involvement with famed Genovese singer-songwriter Gino Paoli produced the international sensation "Senza Fine" (Without End), which propelled her onto the global stage in 1961. Later collaborations included esteemed artists such as Gil Evans, [Herbie Hancock](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/herbie-hancock), and George Benson, as reported by Italy’s ANSA news agency.

Vanoni achieved considerable success at Italy’s prestigious music festivals, participating eight times in the popular Sanremo Music Festival, where she secured second place in 1968 with the song "Casa Bianca."

Her talents extended to songwriting, earning her the coveted Tenco Award twice, making her the only Italian singer to receive the prize as a songwriter and the only woman to win it on two occasions.

![Image 4: Italian singer Ornella Vanoni pictured in Milan, Italy, in 1965](https://static.the-independent.com/2025/11/22/12/Italy_Ornella_Vanoni_61663.jpg)

open image in gallery

Italian singer Ornella Vanoni pictured in Milan, Italy, in 1965(Copyright 1965 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.)

Her biggest commercial success was the song "L'appuntamento" an Italian cover of the Brazilian song "Sentado à beira do caminho" by Erasmo and Roberto Carlos. Originally released in 1970, it experienced a resurrection in popularity after director Steven Soderbergh featured it on the soundtrack of his 2004 film _Ocean's Twelve_, expanding her stardom internationally.

In her later years, Vanoni remained a sought-after guest on television programmes, celebrated for her unpredictable nature, rich collection of anecdotes, and her "complete indifference to political correctness," according to ANSA.

Ornella Vanoni, the revered [Italian](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/italian) singer whose illustrious seven-decade career captivated audiences worldwide with hits such as "Senza Fine" and "L’appuntamento," has died at the age of 91.

[Italian](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/italian) Prime Minister [Giorgia Meloni](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/giorgia-meloni) expressed profound sorrow following the news, stating on X that Vanoni’s "unmistakable voice" had left an indelible mark on Italian culture for generations.

"Italy loses a unique artist who leaves us with an unrepeatable artistic heritage," Meloni remarked.

[_La Stampa_](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/la-stampa) reported that Vanoni passed away from cardiac arrest at her home in [Milan](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/milan).

Known affectionately as "The Lady of Italian Song," Vanoni’s prolific career saw her record over 100 albums, selling more than 55 million copies and cementing her iconic status across multiple generations of fans, according to LaPresse newspaper.

Born in [Milan](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/milan) in 1937, Vanoni initially pursued a passion for theatre, culminating in performances on [Broadway](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/broadway) in 1964.

![Image 3: American actor Rock Hudson hands the "Golden Record" to Italian singer Ornella Vanoni, at a ceremony in the Piccolo Teatro](https://static.the-independent.com/2025/11/22/12/Italy_Ornella_Vanoni_66686.jpg)

open image in gallery

American actor Rock Hudson hands the "Golden Record" to Italian singer Ornella Vanoni, at a ceremony in the Piccolo Teatro(Copyright 1969 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.)

However, her distinctive musical talent, characterised by what _LaPresse_ described as a "highly personal and sophisticated performing style" and a vast repertoire spanning jazz to pop, led her to collaborate with some of Italy’s and the world’s most significant songwriters.

Her partnership and romantic involvement with famed Genovese singer-songwriter Gino Paoli produced the international sensation "Senza Fine" (Without End), which propelled her onto the global stage in 1961. Later collaborations included esteemed artists such as Gil Evans, [Herbie Hancock](https://www.the-independent.com/topic/herbie-hancock), and George Benson, as reported by Italy’s ANSA news agency.

Vanoni achieved considerable success at Italy’s prestigious music festivals, participating eight times in the popular Sanremo Music Festival, where she secured second place in 1968 with the song "Casa Bianca."

Her talents extended to songwriting, earning her the coveted Tenco Award twice, making her the only Italian singer to receive the prize as a songwriter and the only woman to win it on two occasions.

![Image 4: Italian singer Ornella Vanoni pictured in Milan, Italy, in 1965](https://static.the-independent.com/2025/11/22/12/Italy_Ornella_Vanoni_61663.jpg)

open image in gallery

Italian singer Ornella Vanoni pictured in Milan, Italy, in 1965(Copyright 1965 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.)

Her biggest commercial success was the song "L'appuntamento" an Italian cover of the Brazilian song "Sentado à beira do caminho" by Erasmo and Roberto Carlos. Originally released in 1970, it experienced a resurrection in popularity after director Steven Soderbergh featured it on the soundtrack of his 2004 film _Ocean's Twelve_, expanding her stardom internationally.

In her later years, Vanoni remained a sought-after guest on television programmes, celebrated for her unpredictable nature, rich collection of anecdotes, and her "complete indifference to political correctness," according to ANSA.
